_doc: Crop rectangles for slicing the Marriage Report asset sheet into individual PNGs.
Source sheet is 1024x1536; all coordinates are absolute pixels in that sheet.
Two section shapes:
band + outputs[] -> auto-detect N icon bounding boxes across the band (icons are
unevenly spaced, so an even grid split does not work). The
detected count MUST equal outputs.length or the run fails.
rect             -> one explicit crop, for art that touches its neighbour and
cannot be split by a dark gutter.
luma:  pixel brightness at/above which a pixel counts as content during detection.
Icons sitting on a lighter panel (highlights) need a higher value than icons
on flat black (planets).
alpha: [lo, hi] luminance ramp for background keying - at/below lo is fully
transparent, at/above hi is fully opaque, linear between. Feathered rather
than a hard cutoff so the glow around each icon does not get a jagged edge.
DELIBERATELY NOT EXTRACTED:
gemstones - public/gemstones/*.png already ships at 256x256, far better than the
~45px crops available here. Overwriting them would be a downgrade.
zodiac    - data/zodiac.ts already carries all 12 signs as Unicode glyphs, which
is what the sheet draws anyway; crisper at any size and theme-reactive.
anything with baked-in text (score badges, status pills, the label under every
icon) - the app ships 7 languages, so labels stay t() keys.

sections._note: Dark purple silhouette with gold line art - a steep alpha ramp keys the body away, so only true black is dropped and the silhouette stays fully opaque. Bottom edge stops above the decorative divider.

sections._note: Bright gold on flat black, so unlike the couple it takes a steep ramp that drops the background entirely - at [2,14] the near-black plate stayed opaque and read as a dark box sitting on the card.
